prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: GLP-1 is the one candidate that all six of us placed first, and I still think the case holds on the merits rather than on agreement alone. The line from peptide physiology (Holst on the secretion and action of the active forms in humans, Drucker on receptor biology and proglucagon-derived peptides, Mojsov on identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide) to a global therapeutic class is unusually unbroken. The discovery is original, the mechanism is well understood, large randomized outcome trials independently confirm benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease, and the timing is appropriate because the impact is at its peak. A three-person prize on the basic physiology is also the most defensible attribution within the three-name limit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Credit for the early GLP-1 work is contested, with the Mojsov and Habener priority question unresolved in the supplied text, and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's medicinal chemistry (liraglutide, semaglutide) is what made the physiology into drugs. A prize that omits the drug developers risks rewarding physiology while the clinical transformation is industrial. The three-person limit forces an exclusion that some will see as unfair. If the committee judges that translation is the core achievement, my preferred trio is the wrong one.

responses.point: He supports B033 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, but notes that Knudsen's role fits a prize only if translation is rewarded, and he ranks CAR-T second and optogenetics third.
responses.response: I agree that the choice between physiology and drug development is the real decision, and I come down on the physiology side because the Nobel tradition rewards the discovery that enables the medicine. I part company with him on ranking optogenetics above BCR-ABL inhibition. Optogenetics is a very successful method, but I rate B032 higher because it validated a mechanism-based treatment paradigm with decades of survival data, and because a six-way credit crowd for B007 cannot be cleanly cut to three.

responses.point: She ranks TNF blockade (B051) second as a clean two-person prize that established cytokine-targeted therapy in autoimmune disease, and fully mature.
responses.response: Feldmann and Maini form a natural pair and the maturity is not in doubt, so I take B051 seriously as a configuration. My reservation is that the concept of cytokine blockade rests on TNF biology contributed by others who are not credited here, so the intellectual attribution is less complete than she suggests. I still place it below B032 and B026 because those have clearer single mechanisms, but I would not oppose it as a second part if the committee wanted a two-part prize.

responses.point: As chair he proposes June and Sadelain for CAR-T, noting that Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy is a distinct line and Eshhar's early chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names.
responses.response: I agree that June and Sadelain are the strongest pair and that Rosenberg belongs to a different line. I would go further and say that the missing Eshhar credit weakens B026 as a prize candidate more than he indicates, since the chimeric receptor concept is the invention, and we cannot credit it with the names supplied. That is why I put it third rather than second. It remains a serious alternative if the committee is content to credit design and clinical proof.

responses.point: He places nusinersen (B045) third as a clean two-person configuration that turned a lethal infant disease into a treatable one, while noting it may be slightly early.
responses.response: I rank B045 fourth, and we are close. The mechanism-to-medicine story with Krainer and Bennett is elegant. I accept his point on timing, but what holds me back is that the SMN gene discovery and the clinical program contributors fall outside the credited names, and the platform's generality is still being demonstrated. It is a good future candidate, but for this year I see less urgency than for B033 or B032.

uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen, and the position of Habener and other early GLP-1 groups, is not resolved by the supplied evidence.
Whether a two-part prize pairing B033 with a second achievement would be preferable to a single GLP-1 prize is unsettled, and the three-person limit would then force cutting the GLP-1 trio.
I cannot verify the detailed priority history of the early GLP-1 literature from the supplied materials.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate on the shortlist involves my own work. My profile records a co-authored spatial transcriptomics paper and co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg, but none of the shortlisted candidates concerns those subjects, so no specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile.
